title: Cosmological natural selection
example_questions: Why are the laws of physics fine tuned?
What if every black hole made a new universe?
summary: Each black hole spawns a new universe whose physical constants are slightly mutated from its parent's. Universes whose constants favour black holes leave more offspring, so a typical universe should be tuned to make many black holes. This offers an evolutionary explanation for why constants look fine tuned.
support_note: Makes testable predictions but has few supporters.
what_happens: Each black hole births a child universe
Over generations, black hole friendly universes dominate
objections: The mechanism for creating universes in black holes is assumed, not derived

sources.title: The status of cosmological natural selection
